proposed_comments.title: Read Robocopy settings from the module settings file

confidence.rationale: The current upstream line calls GetSettings without RobocopyUISettings.ModuleName, while the settings type defines a module file used by the UI toggle.

proposed_comments.body: **High:** `SaveOptionsButton_Click` reads `RobocopyUISettings` without the Robocopy UI module name, so the legacy-save toggle is loaded from the root settings file instead of the module settings file. On a normal profile this leaves `UseLegacySaveMode` at its default or can fail to deserialize the intended module settings, so the setting exposed by this PR is not honored when saving `.rcj` files. Please read the module-specific settings file, for example by using `GetSettingsOrDefault<RobocopyUISettings>(RobocopyUISettings.ModuleName)`, before choosing the legacy save path.

proposed_comments.title: Stop the launch event listener while Robocopy UI is disabled

confidence.rationale: The current upstream constructor starts the public launch-event waiter and disable only flips _enabled, leaving the callback able to call StartProcess after disable and without process-handle synchronization.

proposed_comments.body: **High:** The constructor starts the named `ROBOCOPY_UI_LAUNCH_EVENT` waiter before the module is enabled, and the callback calls `StartProcess()` without checking `_enabled`. Since `disable()` only flips `_enabled` and never stops the waiter, any process that signals the public launch event can still start Robocopy UI while the module is disabled; the callback can also race with `disable()` over `m_process`. Please start the waiter only from `enable()`, stop it from `disable()`, ignore non-success callbacks, and serialize access to the tracked process handle.
